title: Appendices
body:
## A. Glossary of Optical Components Terminology

**CATV (Community Antenna Television).** Industry shorthand for the cable-television distribution segment; in AAOI's context it denotes the business of supplying optical transmitters, amplifiers, and nodes to cable operators. CATV represented 53.8% of FY2025 revenue, channelled primarily through the Digicomm distribution relationship.

**CPO (Co-Packaged Optics).** A next-generation packaging architecture in which optical engines are mounted directly on the same substrate as the switch ASIC, eliminating the pluggable cage and shrinking the electrical trace between silicon and fibre. CPO is the anticipated successor to pluggable 1.6T modules for future switch generations, though volume timelines remain contested across hyperscalers.

**DOCSIS (Data Over Cable Service Interface Specification).** The protocol stack governing data exchange between cable modems and headend equipment over HFC plants; DOCSIS 3.1 and 4.0 target symmetrical multi-gigabit consumer services. AAOI's CATV transmitters feed the optical nodes that connect HFC distribution plant to cable headends.

**DFB (Distributed Feedback Laser).** A semiconductor laser in which a diffraction grating embedded along the gain medium provides wavelength-selective optical feedback, producing stable single-longitudinal-mode emission. DFBs are the workhorse light source for CATV transmitters and for single-mode datacenter links at speeds up to 100G per lane.

**DSP-CDR (Digital Signal Processor / Clock-Data Recovery).** The silicon die inside a high-speed pluggable transceiver responsible for clock recovery, channel equalisation, forward-error correction, and analogue-digital conversion; typically the dominant power consumer in an 800G module. DSP-CDRs are generally sourced from Marvell, Broadcom, or Credo rather than manufactured in-house by optical vendors such as AAOI.

**EML (Electro-absorption Modulated Laser).** A monolithically integrated InP device combining a DFB laser with an electro-absorption modulator on a single chip, enabling 50G-to-100G-per-lane modulation at lower drive voltage than external lithium-niobate modulators. AAOI manufactures EMLs in-house as part of its wafer-to-module vertical stack.

**HFC (Hybrid Fiber-Coaxial).** The access-network architecture used by cable operators worldwide, in which fibre runs from the headend to neighbourhood optical nodes and coaxial cable covers the final subscriber drop. AAOI's CATV segment expands when operators upgrade HFC nodes to carry DOCSIS 3.1/4.0 capacity.

**MBE (Molecular Beam Epitaxy).** An ultra-high-vacuum deposition technique that grows compound semiconductor layers one atomic monolayer at a time with exceptional compositional precision. AAOI operates proprietary MBE reactors internally — a capital-intensive capability that most fabless transceiver designers outsource to contract foundries.

**MOCVD (Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition).** A complementary epitaxial technique using organometallic precursor gases to deposit III-V semiconductor layers at higher throughput than MBE; preferred for volume production of laser wafers. AAOI deploys both MBE and MOCVD across its Sugar Land and Ningbo fabs, anchoring vertical integration from raw wafer to finished module.

**OSFP (Octal Small Form-factor Pluggable).** An 8-lane pluggable transceiver housing standardised for 400G and 800G aggregate throughput (8 × 50G or 8 × 100G per lane), with a slightly larger footprint than QSFP-DD that accommodates higher thermal dissipation. OSFP and QSFP-DD co-exist as the dominant form factors for AI-cluster switch ports at 800G.

**QSFP-DD (Quad Small Form-factor Pluggable Double Density).** An 8-lane pluggable transceiver backwards-compatible with QSFP28/QSFP56 host sockets, supporting 400G and 800G aggregate speeds; the "-DD" suffix denotes double the electrical contacts of legacy QSFP housings. Mechanical compatibility with existing cage infrastructure made QSFP-DD a preferred form factor in hyperscale network refreshes.

**VCSEL (Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser).** A laser that emits light perpendicular to the wafer surface, enabling wafer-scale testing and low-cost high-density arrays. VCSELs dominate short-reach multimode links within a rack or campus but lack the output power and reach for the single-mode intra-datacenter distances where AAOI's InP-based DFBs and EMLs compete.

## B. Quarterly Revenue — Six-Quarter Sequential Growth Period

The table below captures the six-quarter run from Q3 2024 through Q4 2025, the period in which AAOI inflected from a cyclical trough toward its strongest annual result on record. Segment data for Q3 and Q4 2025 are drawn from the [Q3 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774925033627/aaoi20250930_10q.htm) and the [Q4/FY2025 earnings press release](https://investors.ao-inc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-optoelectronics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-5) respectively; earlier quarters reflect consolidated figures from the same filings.

| Quarter | Revenue ($M) | QoQ Δ | CATV ($M) | Datacenter ($M) | GAAP Gross Margin |
|---------|-------------|--------|-----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Q3 2024 | 65.2 | — | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q4 2024 | 100.3 | +53.8% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q1 2025 | 99.9 | −0.4% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q2 2025 | 103.0 | +3.1% | n/d | n/d | n/d |
| Q3 2025 | 118.6 | +15.1% | 70.6 | 43.9 | 28.0% |
| Q4 2025 | 134.3 | +13.2% | 54.0 | 74.9 | ~30%* |

*Q4 2025 GAAP gross margin implied from the FY2025 full-year figure of 30.0% reported in the [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm). Q4 2025 marked the first quarter in which datacenter revenue exceeded CATV — a mix shift management cited as structurally significant entering FY2026. *n/d* = not separately disclosed in the relevant filing for that period.

## C. Primary Source Registry

**SEC Filings**

- [FY2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm) — Filed March 2026 for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2025. Principal source for full-year revenue ($455.7M), segment mix, customer concentration (Digicomm 53.1%, Microsoft 28.8%), headcount (4,691), IP portfolio, manufacturing footprint, accumulated deficit ($493.1M), and the Amazon warrant description.

- [Q3 2025 Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000143774925033627/aaoi20250930_10q.htm) — Filed November 2025 for the quarter ended 30 September 2025. Source for Q3 2025 segment revenue detail (CATV $70.6M, datacenter $43.9M), GAAP gross margin of 28.0%, non-GAAP gross margin of 31.0%, and nine-month year-to-date financial statements.

**Earnings 8-K Exhibits (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.01)**

- [Q4 and Full-Year 2025 Earnings Release — EDGAR Exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000168316826003562/aaoi_ex9901.htm) — Exhibit 99.01 to the Form 8-K reporting Q4 2025 results; source for Q4 2025 quarterly revenue ($134.3M), datacenter/CATV segment split, and management commentary on the datacenter-exceeding-CATV inflection.

- [Q4 and Full-Year 2024 Earnings Release — EDGAR Exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158114/000168316825008029/aaoi_ex9901.htm) — Exhibit 99.01 to the Form 8-K reporting Q4 2024 results; source for FY2024 revenue ($249.4M), FY2024 GAAP gross margin (24.8%), FY2024 net loss ($186.7M), and prior-year customer concentration comparisons.

**Investor Relations Press Releases**

- [Applied Optoelectronics Reports Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2025 Results](https://investors.ao-inc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-optoelectronics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-5) — IR-hosted version of the Q4/FY2025 earnings release; includes management quotations regarding the datacenter ramp and 1.6T product introduction cited throughout this dossier.

- [Applied Optoelectronics Reports Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Results](https://investors.ao-inc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-optoelectronics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-4) — IR-hosted version of the Q4/FY2024 earnings release; baseline comparator for year-over-year revenue and margin growth narratives.
